new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Spot-checked all four 'silent' supplementary works (JIPA ms, Bossers & Boone 2023, NLLT preprint + NLLT text, balafon paper) by a full-text search for stress/accent|accent|prominen|intonation|metrical|foot|feet|tonic: none says anything about word stress in Northern Toussian; the only hits are Bossers & Boone's tone-diacritic sentence (PDF p. 8), the NLLT metrical-grid analogy (preprint PDF p. 29) and 'intonational boundary tones'. Nothing missed for nort2787. The only stress-adjacent remark anywhere held by the project is Prost 1964's 'position inaccentuée' / 'ə atone' vowel-reduction note, which concerns Southern Toussian (wib) and was correctly excluded.

sources.citation: Struthers-Young, Anthony. 2025. Double downstep in Northern Toussian: Implications on tonal representation. Natural Language & Linguistic Theory 43: 2969-3025. doi:10.1007/s11049-025-09666-4 (CC-BY)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Section 2.2 'Basic tonology' (pp. 2975-2976): three contrastive level tones H, M, L; CV syllables bear two- and three-tone contours; no consistent melody mapping in nouns; little declination in H/M sequences. The word 'stress' occurs only once, in a theoretical aside about metrical grids (Hayes 1995), not about Northern Toussian.

Sections: Consonants, Vowels (incl. pharyngeal vowels), Tone (pp. 18-25: three level tones H/M/L, six lexical contour tones, downstep, double downstep), consonant clusters/codas, transcription of a passage. sources.note: Different dialect (Kourinion) from the dissertation (Djigouera). Silent on stress. Its extra-high + xHH-contour analysis is explicitly reanalysed as an HM contour by Struthers-Young (JIPA ms p. 21) - a tone-inventory disagreement, not a stress one.

sources.citation: Bossers, Hannah & Carin Boone. 2023. Esquisse phonologique du toussian du nord. Ouagadougou: SIL Burkina Faso. 59 pp. (Kourinion dialect)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress/accent. Ch. 2 syllable and word structure (most simple words monosyllabic: 61.7% of nouns, 89% of verbs), ch. 3-4 segments, ch. 6 'Ton' (p. 39): mora is the TBU; three phonemic tone levels H, M, B plus a distributionally limited extra-high xH. The only hits for 'accent' are the diacritic marks on TBUs; no 'intensité', 'proéminence' or 'accentué' in the text.

sources.harvard_location: Tozzer Library (offsite storage), call number L.SOC.42.105.28.7.65 (70)
sources.note: Describes SOUTHERN Toussian (Win, Toussiana), not nort2787. §22 'Les tons': three tones, notation only relative. Incidental mentions of 'accent' as a phonetic feature: 'Je crois que tout a accentué et allongé prend la glottalisation' and ɛ/e 'peuvent en position inaccentuée devenir ə' (p. 253) — no rule for where accent falls. The Northern-dialect notes (pp. 319-327) are not in these excerpts.
